name: Isabel Cross-System Event Transport
purpose: Provide one real-time event contract between browser, Unreal, voice, screens, brain, memory, approvals and execution without conflicting state ownership.

transport_model.clock: server-issued UTC timestamp plus monotonic session sequence

screens: screen content health and last-good route
memory: memory availability and approved durable records
approvals: approval status for exact payload hashes
system: canonical state version and session sequence

conflict_resolution.rule_1: No subsystem may directly overwrite a field owned by another subsystem.
conflict_resolution.rule_2: All state changes are requests validated against field ownership and invariants.
conflict_resolution.rule_3: Higher sequence wins only within the same owned field and connection epoch.
conflict_resolution.rule_4: Older connection epochs cannot overwrite newer session state.
conflict_resolution.rule_5: Duplicate idempotency keys are acknowledged but not re-applied.
conflict_resolution.rule_6: Consequential actions require an approval event whose payload hash still matches.
conflict_resolution.rule_7: Execution completion never implies verification completion.

race_conditions_to_block: browser reconnect overwriting newer Unreal posture
late TTS completion restarting speech after interruption
stale navigation completion moving Isabel after replanning
screen recovery replacing a newer screen route
old approval authorizing a changed payload
duplicate execution request replaying an external action
out-of-order memory response replacing newer session context
saturday_validation: rapidly issue LOOK_AT_USER then GO_TO_SCREEN_02 and prove stale look completion cannot cancel navigation
interrupt TTS mid-sentence and prove late audio-complete event cannot resume mouth movement
refresh browser and prove connection epoch increments without resetting work thread
drop SCREEN_02 then restore it and prove other screens remain live
change an approved payload and prove execution is blocked until re-approved
send duplicate execution request and prove idempotency prevents replay
